title: Tangent initial ideal of a normally flat regular-center pair
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
There are canonical graded surjections $\beta:B\twoheadrightarrow S$, $X_i\mapsto([\bar x_i]_1\otimes1)$, and $\gamma:k[X_0,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$, sending variables to the corresponding degree-one classes. The parameter map identifies $k[X,Y]$ with $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T$, and if $C=\ker\beta$, then
$$\ker\gamma=C\,k[X,Y].$$
In particular the kernel of the tangent graded quotient is the extension of the equations of the normal-cone fibre, for these specified parameter maps.

source.place: Ancillary source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), section 2, p.153, normal-flat tangent/normal-cone comparison, and the paragraph after Example (4.2), p.157; the cited underlying result is Resolution of singularities (1964), Chapter II, Theorem 2; https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13, p.94, is ancestor motivation only. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
The chosen parameters generate $\mathfrak M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], their full list is regular, its $x$-prefix is regular, and $A=T/P$ is regular local of dimension $s$, with maximal ideal generated by the images of the $y_j$. Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] first to the full list and then to its $x$-prefix. This gives, for the specified parameter maps,
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y],\qquad \operatorname{gr}_{P}T=A[X].$$
For the prefix, regularity is the prefix condition in the definition of a regular sequence. In the first identity $T/\mathfrak M=k$; in the second $T/P=A$.

Products of $d$ generators of $I$ generate $I^d$, so their classes span $G_d$ over $A$. Their tensors with $1$ span $S_d$ over $k$: expand any tensor as a finite sum and use the balancing relation. The polynomial universal property therefore gives the displayed graded surjection $\beta$. In the same way, products of $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m$ span $\mathfrak m^d/\mathfrak m^{d+1}$ over $k$, giving the displayed graded surjection $\gamma$. The assignments preserve multiplication because multiplying classes of representatives is the associated-graded product. In degree zero both maps are the identity of $k$; $C=\ker\beta$ is homogeneous because $\beta$ preserves degrees.

source.place: Elementary products-of-generators argument; associated-graded conventions of section 00JL (section-graded).

proof.text:
Fix $d\geq0$ and let $K_d$ be the kernel of $A[X]_d\twoheadrightarrow G_d$. Each $G_d$ is flat over $A$: it is a direct summand of the flat module $G$, and tensoring an injection with that summand is injective by composing its split inclusion with the injective tensor map for $G$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] applied to
$$0\longrightarrow K_d\longrightarrow A[X]_d\longrightarrow G_d\longrightarrow0$$
and $k$ gives an exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow K_d\otimes_Ak\longrightarrow k[X]_d\longrightarrow S_d\longrightarrow0.$$
Here tensoring the monomial basis identifies $A[X]_d\otimes_Ak$ with $k[X]_d$; the last map sends $X^\alpha$ to the tensor of the class of $\bar x^\alpha$, so it is exactly $\beta_d$. Consequently every $H\in C_d$ is a finite $k$-linear combination of reductions of elements of $K_d$.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); explicit degreewise kernel after tensoring, using the parameter identification from step 1.

proof.text:
For $u\in K_d\subset A[X]_d$, choose lifts to $T$ of its finitely many coefficients and let $t=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}a_\alpha x^\alpha\in P^d$. Since $u$ maps to zero in $I^d/I^{d+1}$, the image of $t$ in $R$ belongs to $I^{d+1}$. Choose $v\in P^{d+1}$ with that same image. Then $f=t-v\in\mathfrak a\cap P^d$. Modulo $\mathfrak M^{d+1}$, all coefficients $a_\alpha$ may be reduced modulo $\mathfrak M$, and $v$ vanishes. Thus the degree-$d$ class of $f$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$ is precisely $u\bmod\mathfrak n$, viewed in $k[X]_d$; this class maps to zero under $\gamma$. Step 3 now gives $C_d\subseteq\ker\gamma$ for every $d$. Summing homogeneous components and multiplying by arbitrary polynomials gives
$$C\,k[X,Y]\subseteq\ker\gamma.$$
Therefore $\gamma$ factors through a graded surjection $\phi:S[Y]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$. The identification of its source sends the class of $X_i$ to $\beta(X_i)$ and preserves $Y_j$; it follows directly by taking coefficients of $Y$-monomials modulo $C$.

source.place: Elementary representative calculation using the exact sequence in step 3; polynomial quotients computed coefficient by coefficient.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-normal-flat-hilbert-convolution] with the Noetherian local ring $R=T/\mathfrak a$, the ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and its regular local quotient $A$ of dimension $s$ from step 1. Its flatness hypothesis is exactly the assumed flatness of $G$ over $A$. Writing $h_j=\dim_k S_j$, it gives
$$\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^n h_j\binom{n-j+s}{s}.$$
By [lem-trf-maximal-adic-graded-length-bridge] the left side is $\sum_{d=0}^n\dim_k(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)_d$. The right side is $\sum_{d=0}^n\dim_k(S[Y])_d$: for each basis vector of $S_j$, use all $Y$-monomials of total degree at most $n-j$. Their number is $\binom{n-j+s}{s}$, by adding a slack exponent and placing $s$ separators among $n-j+s$ positions. For $s=0$ there is exactly one such monomial. All these vector spaces are finite-dimensional.

source.place: Agent numerical assembly of Hironaka (1970), p.157, normal-flat product Hilbert identity; ILO VIII 2.3.13 is only ancestor motivation. The numerical theorem is cited as its own node, not assumed as an elementary calculation.

proof.text:
For every $n$, the direct sum of $\phi_d$ over $0\leq d\leq n$ is a surjection between finite-dimensional vector spaces of equal dimension by step 5. Its kernel is zero (lift a basis of the target; the same number of independent lifts already forms a basis of the source). Hence every $\phi_d$ is injective. Every element of a graded ring is a finite sum of homogeneous elements, so $\phi$ is injective and therefore an isomorphism. The factorization of the specified map $\gamma$ in step 4 now gives
$$\ker\gamma=C\,k[X,Y],$$
as claimed. The construction kept the specified images of every $X_i$ and $Y_j$, so it proves the required equality of ideals for those parameter maps.

source.place: Elementary finite-dimensional linear algebra and the explicit factorization of step 4; concludes the parameter-specific comparison of Hironaka (1970), pp.153,157.

lean.statement: theorem normalFlatDoubleInitialIdeal {T : Type u} [CommRing T] [IsRegularLocalRing T] (r s : ℕ) (x : Fin (r + 1) → T) (y : Fin s → T) (hparams : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)) (a : Ideal T) (ha : a ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range x)) [Module.Flat ((T ⧸ a) ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)) (Ideal.associatedGraded ((Ideal.span (Set.range x)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)))] : Function.Surjective (normalFlatBeta x y hparams a ha) ∧ Function.Surjective (normalFlatGamma x y hparams a) ∧ Function.Bijective (normalFlatAmbientMap x y hparams) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (r + 1)) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField T)), p.IsHomogeneous n → normalFlatBeta x y hparams a ha p ∈ Submodule.span (IsLocalRing.ResidueField T) (Set.range (normalFlatParameterClass x y hparams a ha n))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (r + 1) ⊕ Fin s) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField T)), p.IsHomogeneous n → ∃ b : Ideal.associatedGradedPiece ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)) n, normalFlatGamma x y hparams a p = DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a))) n b) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (r + 1) ⊕ Fin s) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField T)), p.IsHomogeneous n → ∃ b : Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T) n, normalFlatAmbientMap x y hparams p = DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal T)) n b) ∧ RingHom.ker (normalFlatGamma x y hparams a) = (RingHom.ker (normalFlatBeta x y hparams a ha)).map (MvPolynomial.rename Sum.inl)
lean.note: Canonical parameter maps are constructed by polynomial evaluation. The fibre uses k tensor_(R/I) gr_I R, canonically tensor-symmetric to the displayed G tensor_A k.
